lines.text: Today you will learn the most important money question of all: do I need it, or do I want it?
A need is something you must have to live safely, stay healthy and learn.
Food, water, clothes, a home, medicine and school books are needs.
Needs come first in every money plan.
A want is something nice to have, but you can live without it.
Toys, video games, chocolates and fancy stickers are wants.
Wants are fine, once the needs are covered.
The same thing can be a need or a want.
One pair of school shoes is a need, but a fourth pair of shiny shoes is a want.
Ask yourself: what happens if I do not buy it?
Money spent on one thing cannot be spent on another.
If Aarav spends ₹100 on a toy car, he gives up the ₹100 comic he also liked.
The thing you give up is the real cost of your choice.
Before you spend, ask yourself four quick questions.
Do I need this to be safe, healthy or to learn, and what happens if I do not buy it?
Can I wait a week, and will I still want it then?
And finally, what will I give up if I buy it?
Zoya has fifty rupees, and the ice cream cart is right outside her school.
The ice cream costs forty rupees, but her brother’s birthday gift costs fifty rupees.
If she buys the ice cream, she gives up the gift for her brother.
Zoya decides to wait, because the gift matters more to her today.
Your class is going to the zoo, and you have five hundred rupees.
First the needs: the bus, the entry ticket, lunch and water come to three hundred and fifty rupees.
That leaves one hundred and fifty rupees, and we keep fifty rupees safe for an emergency.
Now you can choose wants with the last one hundred rupees.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
